senses: to turn one's attention to, focus (on)
la:verb:intendo.html:
in-tendo, di, tum and sum, 3, v. a. (
part. intenditus, Mai.), to stretch out or forth, extend.
Lit.
In hunc intende digitum, hic lenost, point in scorn, : dextram ad statuam,: alicui manus,: bracchia,: manus,: jubet intendi bracchia velis,: intenta bracchia remis, id. ib, 5, 136: ventis vela,: nervos aut remittere,: cutem,: jamque manus Colchis crinemque intenderat astris,.—
To bend a bow, etc.: ballistam in aliquem,: arcum,: intentus est arcus in me unum,.—
To aim or direct at a thing: tela in patriam,: tela intenta jugulis civitatis,: sagittam,: telum in jugulum,.—
To stretch or spread out; to stretch, lay or put upon a thing: tabernacula carbaseis intenta velis,pitched,; : sella intenta loris,: stuppea vincula collo Intendunt,: duro intendere bracchia tergo,i. e. to bind with the cestus,: locum sertis,encircled, surrounded,: vela secundi Intendunt Zephyri,swell, fill,: intendentibus tenebris,spreading,.—
Trop.
To strain or stretch towards, to extend: aciem acrem in omnes partes intendit,turns keen looks on every side,: aciem longius,: quo intendisset oculos,whithersoever he turns his eyes,: aures ad verba,: cum putaret licere senatui, et mitigare leges et intendere, to stretch, i. e. increase the rigor of, : numeros intendere nervis, (per nervos intentos, Forbig.); cf.: strepitum fidis intendisse Latinae,.—
Esp.
To direct towards any thing, to turn or bend in any direction: digna est res ubi tu nervos intendas tuos,: intendenda in senem est fallacia,: ut eo quo intendit, cum exercitu mature perveniat,: iter, to direct one's course: ad explorandum quonam hostes iter intendissent,: a porta ad praetorem iter intendit,: coeptum iter in Italiam,; .—Absol.: quo nunc primum intendam,whither shall I turn?.—
Intendere animum, to direct one's thoughts or attention to any thing: quaero enim non quibus intendam rebus animum, sed, etc., ap. : parum defigunt animos et intendunt in ea, quae, etc.,: quo animum intendat, facile perspicio,; Liv. praef. 9: intentus animus tuus est ad fortissimum virum liberandum,: oculi mentesque ad pugnam intentae,: in ea re omnium nostrorum intentis animis,: intendere animum in regnum Adherbalis,: ad bellum animum intendit,: animum studiis et rebus honestis,: considerationem in aliquam rem,: omnes cogitationes ad aliquid,: omnium eo curae sunt intentae,; : ad scribendum animum, oculos, manum,: ubi ingenium intenderis, valet, : eruditionem tuam,. —
Hence, intendere alone, to urge on, incite: intenderant eum ad cavendi omnia curam tot auditae proditiones,: aliquem ad custodiae curam,: vis omnis intendenda rebus,.—
To enlarge, spread, extend, magnify: intendetur socordia, si nullus ex se metus aut spes,: amici accendendis offensionibus callidi, intendere vera. adgerere falsa,exaggerated,; 4, 11: gloriam,; 12, 35: tormentum,—
Absol., to turn one's attention to, exert one's self for, to purpose, endeavor, intend: pergin, sceleste, intendere hanc arguere? Brix: quod est tibi ante explicandum, quam illuc proficiscare, quo te dicis intendere,: quod ubi secus procedit, neque quod intenderat, efficere potest,: quocumque intenderat,; cf. ; 102, 1: genera lectionum, quae praecipue convenire intendentibus, ut oratores fiant,: ad nuptias,.—
With inf.: quo ire intenderant,: altum petere intendit,.—
Intendere se, to exert one's self, prepare for any thing: se ad firmitatem,: se in rem,: qui se intenderunt adversarios in ejus tribunatum, Cael. ap. .—
Intendere animo, to purpose in one's mind, to intend: si C. Antonius, quod animo intenderat, perficere potuisset,.—
To maintain, assert: eam sese intendit esse,.—Esp., as leg. t. t., to aver, maintain, assert as a plaintiff in court: quo modo nunc intendit,: si quod intendit adversarius tuus, probationibus implere non possit, Vet. cujusd. Jurec. Consult. 6, 16 Huschke; . —
To threaten with any thing, to seek to bring upon, to afflict with: alicui actionem perduellionis,: alicui litem,: periculum in omnes,: crimen in aliquem,: injuriarum formulam,: probra et minas alicui,: metum intendere,.—
Intendere in se, to contemplate one's self: quid sit Deus: totus in se intendat, an ad nos aliquando respiciat, praef. 1.—
Intendere alicui, to be intended for a person, —
In rhet., to premise, to state as the proposition of a syllogism, .—
In gram., to make long, to use (a syllable) as long: primam syllabam intendit, tertiam corripuit,. 18. — Hence, P. a. in two forms.
inten-tus, a, um.
On the stretch, strained, bent: arcus,; .—
Attentive to, intent upon, waiting for something.
With dat.: quem pueri intenti ludo exercent,: intentus recipiendo exercitui esse,.—
With abl.: aliquo negotio intentus,; ; 54.—
Absol., eager, intent: at Romani domi militiaeque intenti festinare,: senatus nihil sane intentus,: intenti exspectant signum,: intenti ora tenebant,: totam causam quam maxime intentis, quod aiunt, oculis contemplari,: intentaque tuis precibus se praebuit aure,. — Comp.: intentiore custodia aliquem asservare,.—Sup.: cum intentissima conquisitione ad triginta milia peditum confecisset,: intentissima cura aliquid consequi,: haec omnia intentissima cura acta,. —
Strict: intentum et magnis delictis inexorabilem scias,: intentius delectum habere,: intentiorem fore disciplinam,.—
Raised: intento alimentorum pretio,. —
Of speech and style, vigorous, nervous: sermo,: pars orationis,. — Adv.: in-tentē, with earnestness, attentively, intently: pronuntiare,: audire,.— Comp. (cf. intense): cum delectus intentius haberetur,: et quo intentius custodiae serventur,: apparare proelium,: se excusare,: premere obsessos,: adesse alicui rei,.—Sup.: exspectans intentissime,. —
intensus, a, um.
Stretched,

tightened, tight: per intensos funes ire, Sen. de Ira, 2, 13.—

Violent: intensior impetus,: virtus in mediocribus modice intensior,.—
Attentive; sup., — Adv.: intensē, violently; comp.: intensius, Fronto de Fer. Als. 3 Mai.; Schol. ; sup.: intensissime,.

la:verb:intellego.gloss: to understand, comprehend, realize, come to know
senses: to understand, comprehend, realize, come to know
to perceive, discern, see, observe, recognise; feel, notice
la:verb:intellego.html:
intellĕgo (less correctly intellĭgo), exi, ectum (intellexti for intellexisti, ; :
intellexes for intellexisses,; subj. perf.: intellegerint, Dietsch), 3, v. a.
inter-lego
, to see into, perceive, understand.
Lit.
To perceive, understand, comprehend: qualem autem deum intellegere nos possumus nulla virtute praeditum, Schoemann ad loc.: haec dumtaxat in Graecis intellego, quae ipsi, qui scripserunt, voluerunt a vulgo intellegi,: puderet me dicere non intellegere, si vos ipsi intellegeretis, qui ista defenditis,: corpus quid sit intellego,: quare autem in his vis deorum insit, tum intellegam cum cognovero,: quam sis audax hinc omnes intellegere potuerunt, quod,: magna ex parvis,: intellexi ex tuis litteris, te audisse,: de gestu intellego, quid respondeas,: intellegere et sapere plus quam ceteros,: cernere aliquid animo atque intellegere,: facile intellectu est,: intellegi necesse est: esse deos,; : quocirca intellegi necesse est, in ipsis rebus invitamenta inesse,.—In answers, intellego corresponds to our I understand, go on, very well, ; .— Abl. absol.: intellecto; with rel. clause: quidam bonorum caesi, postquam, intellecto in quos saeviretur, pessimi quoque arma rapuerant,; intellecto quantum bellum suscitaret,.—
In partic., to have an accurate knowledge of or skill in a thing, to be a connoisseur: faciunt intellegendo ut nihil intellegant,: tametsi non multum in istis rebus intellego,: hoc nugatorium sciebam esse, ista intellegere,, § 33: quoniam non intellexerunt in operibus domini,: illi qui linguam ejus intellegebant,; .—
To distinguish: oraculorum praestigias profani a veritate intellegere non possunt,.—
To see, perceive, observe by the understanding: vehementer nunc mihi est irata: sentio atque intellego,: ubi neque cohortationes suas neque preces audiri intellegit,: illi, ante inito, ut intellectum est, consilio,: intellego, quid loquar,.—
Of persons, to understand, comprehend, judge rightly (post-Aug.): quod Catonem aetas sua parum intellexisset,: quando Socrates ab hominibus sui temporis parum intellegebatur,; ; : quem legatum tribunus ita et intellexit et cepit, ut, etc.,. —
To understand a language: isti qui linguam avium intellegunt, Pac. ap. (Trag. v. 83 Rib.): in iis linguis quas non intellegimus,: quantum ego Graece scripta intellegere possum,: linguam ejus,; .—
To understand by any thing, to take a thing to mean.
With in or sub aliqua re, or per aliquid: illa est εὐταξία, in qua intellegitur ordinis conservatio, : sub hoc themate intellegere non hoc, sed, etc.,: intellego sub hoc verbo multa,: per nemo homo,: solem sub appellatione Jovis,: per sagittas vim radiorum,. —
With two acc.: non habeo quod intellegam bonum illud,. —
With acc. and abl.: consuetudo omnibus his nominibus Argesten intellegi, .—
Transf., to perceive, discern by the senses; to see, feel, notice. Alcumenam ante aedis stare saturam intellego, : Si. Statum vide hominis, Callipho.... Ca. Bene confidenterque astitisse intellego, : illa quidem primo nullos intellegit ignes,: frigus,: vestigia hominum intellegi a feris,; .— Hence, in-tellĕgens, entis, P. a., that has understanding or that understands a thing; intelligent, acquainted with.
In gen.: semperne vulgi judicium cum intellegentium judicio congruit?: intellegens dicendi existimator,: judicium,: vir,.—With gen.: cujusvis generis ejus intellegens,.—Comp.: aliquid intellegentiore mente discutere,.—
In partic.
Intellegens alicujus, that understands a person, rightly estimates his character: intellegens principis nostri, cujus videbam hanc esse laudem, Döring ad loc.—
Well skilled in matters of taste, a connoisseur: signa pulcherrima quae non modo istum hominem, ingeniosum atque intellegentem, verum etiam quemvis nostrum, quos iste idiotas appellat, delectare possent,: ut putetur in istis rebus intellegens esse,. 4, 15, § 33.—Adv.: intellĕgenter, intelligently: ut amice, ut intelligenter, ut attente audiamur,: lectitare,.

la:prep:inter.html:
inter, adv., and prep. with acc. [kindred to in, intra; Sanscr. antar; Goth. undar; Germ. unter; Engl. under].
Adv., in the midst, in between (poet. and rare): dumque pii petit ora patris stetit arduus inter pontus,: tot montibus inter diviso,; . —
Prep., with acc., between, belwixt, among, amid, surrounded by.
Lit., in space.
Of position only.
Referring to two places or objects, between: qui (mons Jura) est inter Sequanos et Helvetios,: cum inter me et Brundisium Caesar esset,: inter Padum atque Alpes,: ager Tarquiniorum, qui inter urbem ac Tiberim fuit,: locus inter duos lucos,: apud Artemisium inter Euboeam continentemque terram,; so, inter haec maria Asia,.—
Referring to more than two places or objects, among, in the midst of: inter hostium tela versari,: inter multos saucios spe incertae vitae relictus,: rex inter primos constiterat,: inter multitudinem,: inter lignarios,: repertae inter spolia catenae,: vicos aut inter vias manere,: inter ingentes solitudines,: inter deserta ferarum Lustra domosque,.— So, even with a noun in the sing., in the midst of, surrounded by: erat inter ceteram planitiem mons,: tibicines inter exercitum positi,: inter caedem aquila,; cf.: inter ceteram praedam,; : inter purpuram atque aurum,. —
With verbs of motion.
Between, through, among: inter medias stationes hostium erupere,: acies inter bina castra procedunt,; : inter oppositas classes transmisit,: spatiabatur in nemore Parmenion medius inter duces,: medios inter hostes Londinium perrexit,.—
Pregn., including motion to and position between or among things mentioned, among, into the midst of: inter densas, umbrosa cacumina, fagos Adsidue veniebat,: te mea dextera magna inter praemia ducet,: dico te priore nocte venisse inter falcarios in Laecae domum,among the scythe-makers, into the street of the scythe-makers,.—
Transf., of relations conceived as local.
In discrimination (doubt, choice, etc.), between two or more objects: judicium inter deas tres,; cf.: inter Marcellos et Claudios patricios judicare,: inter has sententias dijudicare,: inter diversas opiniones electio, Quint. prooem. 2: discrimen inter gratiosos cives atque fortes,: inter optime valere et gravissime aegrotare nihil prorsus interesse,: qui bellum et pacem inter dubitabant,: trepidare inter scelus metumque,: inter pugnae fugaeque consilium,.—So, with inter repeated: ut nihil inter te atque inter quadrupedem aliquam putes interesse,; : quid intersit inter popularem civem et inter constantem, severum et gravem,.—
In expressing any relation which connects two or more persons, conceived as between or among them (strife, rivalry, friendship, intercourse, etc.).
In gen.: quos inter magna fuit contentio,: Nestor componere lites Inter Peliden festinat et inter Atriden,: certamen inter primores civitates,.—Esp., with pronouns, to express all reciprocal relations, among, with, or between one another; mutually, together: quasi nunc non norimus nos inter nos,; ; ; : quod colloquimur inter nos,with one another,; cf.: inter nos naturā ad civilem communitatem conjuncti sumus,: vobis inter vos voluntatem fuisse conjunctam,: Ciceronis pueri amant inter se, love one another (like the Fr. s'entr'aimer), : inter se consultare,: inter se amare,: neque solum se colent inter se ac diligent,: Di inter se diligunt,: furtim inter se aspiciebant,: complecti inter se lacrimantes milites coepisse,: haec inter se cum repugnent, plerique non vident,: inter se nondum satis noti,: ratio et oratio conciliat homines inter se,: ne nostra nobiscum aut inter nos cessatio vituperetur,: quae res eos in magno diuturnoque bello inter se habuit,.—Sometimes pleon., the reciprocal relation being sufficiently expressed by the context: manus conserentis inter se Romanos exercitus, Dietsch: Ulixes cum Ajace summa vi contendere inter se,: conferti inter se,.—
So of things: ita effici complexiones atomorum inter se,mutual, reciprocal,: colles duos inter se propinquos occupat,near one another,: haud procul inter se erant,: multum inter se distant istae facultates,: res inter se similes,: inter se dissimilis,.—
Of a common privacy, secrecy, etc.: inter nos, between or among ourselves, confidentially, like the Fr. entre nous: nec consulto dicis occulte, sed quod inter nos liceat, ne tu quidem intellegis,: quod inter nos liceat dicere,: quod inter nos sit,but let that be between ourselves,. —
With nouns denoting a multitude of persons, like apud (not ante-Aug.): haudquaquam inter id genus contemptor habebatur,: inter hostes variae fuere sententiae,: credula fama inter gaudentes,: more inter veteres recepto,.—
Of a class of persons or things to which the subject is referred.
In gen., among: homines inter suos nobiles,: inter suos et honestus et nobilis,: in oratoribus vero admirabile est, quantum inter omnes unus excellat,: inter philosophos (Xenophon) reddendus est,: ille Croesus, inter reges opulentissimus,: Borysthenes inter Scythiae amnes amoenissimus,.— So freq. with sup., inter and acc. take the place of a gen.: honestissimus inter suos numerabatur,: plurimum inter eos valere,: maximum imperium inter finitimos,: inter Atheniensīs longe clarissimi,; ; ; ; ; ; .
Esp.: inter paucos, etc.,

among few, i. e. among the few select ones, eminently, especially: pingunt et vestes in Aegypto inter pauca mirabili genere,; cf.: sternutamento utilis inter pauca,: pugna inter paucas memorata populi Romani clades,; cf.: inter paucos disertus,: inter paucos familiarium Neroni assumptus est,: claritudine paucos inter senum regum,; so, inter alios: judicatur inter alios omnes beatus, qui in proelio profuderit animam, among all others to be noticed, i. e. especially, in the highest degree, ; so, inter cuncta,: inter omnia,: inter cetera,.—

In judic. lang., t. t.: inter sicarios, on the charge of assassination: cum praetor quaestionem inter sicarios exercuisset,; ; cf.: in recuperatorio judicio ejus maleficii, de quo inter sicarios quaeritur,: longo intervallo judicium inter sicarios hoc primum committitur,: sexcenti sunt, qui inter sicarios et de veneficiis accusabant,: si ostenderis, quomodo sis eos inter sicarios defensurus,.—
In some idiomatic phrases.
Inter manus, within reach, i. e. close at hand: ante oculos interque manus sunt omnia vestras,; also, upon or in the hands: inter manus domum ablatus,: inter quas (manus) collapsus extinguitur,: inter manus auferri,: inter manus meas crevit,under my hands,: manus inter maestorumque ora parentum,before their faces and within their reach,.—
Inter viam, vias, on the way: dum rus eo, coepi egomet mecum inter vias,; : si se inter viam obtulerit,. —
Of time.
Between two dates or periods specified: dies XLV. inter binos ludos,; .—
During, in the course of, within; for which, in English, we sometimes use by or at: quot prandia inter continuum perdidi triennium,: omnia agentur, quae inter decem annos nefarie flagitioseque facta sunt,; cf.: qui inter annos tot unus inventus sit, quem, etc.,: inter ipsum pugnae tempus,: inter noctem lux orta,: qui plus cernant oculis per noctem quam inter diem,.—
Freq., with substt., to denote an act performed at a certain time, in the course of, while: haec inter cenam Tironi dictavi,at table,; cf.: illuseras heri inter scyphos,: inter fulmina et tonitrua,: promptior inter tenebras affirmatio,: inter initia,at the beginning,.—
During, and hence under the circumstances described, i. e. in spite of, notwithstanding: nobis inter has turbas senatus tamen frequens flagitavit triumphum,amid, in spite of these commotions,: utrumque consilium aspernatus, quod inter ancipitia deterrimum est, dum media sequitur,: senum coloniae inter male parentes et injuste imperantes aegra municipia et discordantia,; cf.: ita neutris cura posteritatis inter infensos vel obnoxios,.—
Inter haec, inter quae, meanwhile, during this time: = interea, inter haec major alius terror,in the mean time,; cf.: inter haec jam praemissi Albam erant equites,; ; ; ; ; : inter quae tribuni plebei petivere, etc.,; ; ; 3, 33; ; : inter quae unctione uti licet,.— So with gerunds and gerundives: inter agendum,at, while,; : inter disceptandum,: inter res agendas,.—
In composition its final r is assimilated in intellego and its derivatives.
Between; as, intercedere, interponere. —
At intervals, from time to time; as, interaestuare, intermittere, intervisere.—
Under, down, to the bottom; as, interire, interficere.

senses: to pass, elapse (in the 3rd person, with time as the subject)
la:verb:intercedo.html:
inter-cēdo, cessi, cessum, 3, v. n.,
to go or come between, to intervene, to be between (syn. intervenio).
Lit.
In gen.: si quis intercedat tertius,: intercedente lunā,: palus intercedebat,: sylvae paludesque intercedebant,: inter singulas legiones impedimentorum magnum numerum intercedere,.—
In partic.
To occur, happen, come to pass: saepe in bello parvis momentis magni casus intercedunt,: inter bellorum curas res parva intercessit,: nullum dictum intercessit,.—
Trop.
Of time, to intervene, pass: vix annus intercesserat, cum, etc.,: intercessere pauci dies,: nox nulla intercessit,: una nox intercesserat,; .—
To be, exist, or come between persons.
In order or rank: etsi nemo intercedebat, etc.,.—
In feelings or conduct: ira inter eas intercessit,: tacebit dum intercedat familiaritas,as long as our friendship lasts,: inter nosmetipsos vetus usus intercedit,: ut ei cum genere humano quasi civile jus intercederet,: nisi intercederent mihi inimicitiae cum istius mulieris viro,: inter nos officia paria intercedunt,; : huic cum reliquis ... bella intercesserant,.—
To interpose one's credit, become surety for a person: promisit, intercessit, dedit,: pro aliquo,,

18, 45: pro aliquo magnam pecuniam,to procure for a person by becoming surety for him,: in omni genere negotiorum et obligationum ... intercedere mulieres prohibentur,. —

To oppose, withstand, protest against; of the tribunes of the people, who interposed their veto against a decree of the senate: cum intercedere vellent rogationi,: nisi mihi levissimus tribunus plebis intercessisset,: ea lege, qua intercedi de provinciis non licebit,: ea quae de reductione regis scripta est auctoritas, cui scis intercessum esse,: praetori,: tribuni plebis intercedentes pro se (Caesare),; cf. At. Cap. ap. . This right of protest was also possessed by other magistrates; v. Varr. ap. ; Ascon. ap. Pis. 26; .—So fig.: si status condictus cum hoste intercedit dies, tamen est eundum,.—
In gen., to interpose, interfere.
For or in behalf of a person, to intercede, interpose: cum enim vestra auctoritas intercessisset, ut ego regem tuerer,; .—
To obstruct, hinder, interrupt: si nulla aegritudo huic gaudio intercesserit,: intercessit et, quominus in acta sua juraretur, ut ne mensis September Tiberius vocaretur,: de cognomine intercessit Augustus,: non quia intercedendum putem imaginibus,: consilio,: parens noster privatas gratiarum actiones cohibet, intercessurus etiam publicis,: intercedere casibus, occursare fortunae,fin.: iniquitatibus magistratuum,; .

la:adv:interim.gloss: meanwhile, in the meantime, in the interim
senses: meanwhile, in the meantime, in the interim
la:adv:interim.html:
intĕrim, adv.
inter and old acc. of is
.
I.q. interea, meanwhile, in the meantime: ibo intro: tu hic ante aedes interim speculare,: interim dum ante ostium sto,: hoc interim spatio conclave illud concidisse,: quo fugit interim dolor ille?; .—
For a time, for a while (post-Aug.): ut uno interim contenti simus exemplo C. Gracchi,for the moment,: interim admonere illud satis est,; .—
(Cf. interea.) However, nevertheless: interim velim mihi ignescas,: quod alias vitiosum, interim alias rectum est,; —
I. q. nonnumquam, sometimes (post-Aug.): Latinis quidem semper, sed etiam Graecis interim,; so, opp. semper, Sen. de Ira, 2, 21, 8: laturi sententiam indocti saepius atque interim rustici,; ; with nonnumquam,: interim ... interim,sometimes ... sometimes, at one time ... at another,; ; ; : interim ... mox, Dräger.

la:adv:interea.html:
intĕr-ĕā, adv.
Meanwhile, in the meantime, in the interim (class.): saepe interea mihi senex narrabat,: interea dies advenit,: cum interea,; : haec dum Romae geruntur, Quintius interea de agro detruditur,.— With loci: plus triginta natus annis sum, cum interea loci Numquam quicquam facinus feci pejus quam hodie,; ; ; ; Pac. ap. (Trag. Rel. p. 71 Rib.).— *
(For interdum.) Sometimes, .—
Transf., like Engl. meanwhile (approaching the sense of), nevertheless, however (but in class. prose always retaining a reference to time; cf. Krebs, Antibarb. p. 611 sq.),; : cum interea,; cf.: tamen interea,.

la:adj:integer.gloss: complete, whole, intact, uninjured, sound, healthy
senses: complete, whole, intact, uninjured, sound, healthy
la:adj:integer.html:
intĕger, tē^gra, tē^grum (long e in intēgri, intēgros, etc., ; ; ), adj.
2. in and root tag-, tango
,
untouched, unhurt, unchanged.
Lit.
Undiminished, whole, entire, complete, perfect: integer et plenus thensaurus,: exercitus,: annus,: quarum (sublicarum) pars inferior integra remanebat,: integris bonis exulare,: nec superstes Integer,: puer malasque comamque Integer,with beard, and hair on his head,: signa (litterarum),unbroken,.— Adv.: ad integrum, wholly, entirely: corpore carens,. —
Unimpaired, uninjured, unhurt, unwounded, unmutilated, unexhausted, sound, fresh, vigorous.
Absol.: adulescens cum sis, tum, cum est sanguis integer,: aetas,: cum recentes atque integri defessis successissent,; so opp. defessi,; opp. defatigati,; 5, 16; : integris viribus repugnare,: si ad quietem integri iremus, opp. onustus cibo et vino,: integra valetudo,: integrum se salvumque velle,: omnibus rebus integros incolumesque esse,: florentes atque integri,: integros pro sauciis arcessere,; so opp. saucius,: Horatius,: nasus,; ; so opp. truncus,. § 50: cecidit Cethegus integer, et jacuit Catilina cadavere toto,not mutilated,: opes, opp. accisae,: mulier aetate integra,in the flower of her age,: corpora sana et integri sanguinis,; tantum capite integro (opp. transfigurato),unchanged,: quam integerrimis corporibus cibum offerre,free from fever,: antequam ex toto integer fiat,: integra aetate ac valetudine,. —
With gen.: integer aevi sanguis (= integri aevi sanguis, i. e. juvenilis vigor),; ; : integer annorum, (cf. II. A. infra): deos aevi integros, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 440 Vahl.). —
With abl.: fama et fortunis integer,: copiis integra (regio),: neque aetate neque corpore integer,: pectore maturo fuerat puer integer aevo, Ped. : dum vernat sanguis, dum rugis integer annus,—
With a (ab) and abl. (rare): a populi suffragiis integer,i. e. who has not been rejected, D.: cohortes integrae ab labore,: gens integra a cladibus belli,.—
Esp. in phrase ad or in integrum (sc. statum), to a former condition or state: potius quam redeat ad integrum haec eadem oratio,i. e. to have the same story over again,: quod te absente hic filius egit restitui in integrum aequum est,: quos ego non idcirco esse arbitror in integrum restitutos,; : (judicia) in integrum restituit,. —
Not worn, fresh, new, unused: ad integrum bellum cuncta parare,: consilia,: pugnam edere,.—Hence, esp. adv.: de integro, ab integro, ex integro, anew, afresh: ut mihi de integro scribendi causa non sit,; : acrius de integro obortum est bellum,: relata de integro res ad senatum,: columnam efficere ab integro novam,: magnus ab integro saeclorum nascitur ordo,: recipere ex integro vires,: navibus ex integro fabricatis,.—
Untainted, fresh, sweet: ut anteponantur integra contaminatis,: fontes,: sapor,: aper, opp. vitiatus,.—
Not before attempted, fresh: ex integra Graeca integram comoediam Hodie sum acturus,: alias ut uti possim causa hac integra,this pretext as a fresh one,: eum Plautus locum reliquit integrum,not treated, not imitated,.
Trop.
Blameless, irreproachable, spotless, pure, honest, virtuous: cum illo nemo neque integrior esset in civitate, neque sanctior,: (homines) integri, innocentes, religiosi,: integerrima vita,: incorrupti atque integri testes,: vitae,: integer urbis,not spoiled by the city, untainted with city vices,: vir a multis vitiis integer, Sen. de Ira, 1, 18, 3.— Of female chastity: loquere filiam meam quis integram stupraverit,: narratque, ut virgo ab se integra etiam tum siet,: quibus liberos conjugesque suas integras ab istius petulantia conservare non licitum est,: virgines,.—
Of the mind or disposition.
Free from passion or prejudice, unbiassed, impartial: integrum se servare, to keep one's self neutral, : arbiter,: scopulis surdior Icari Voces audit, adhuc integer,untouched with love, heart-whole,: bracchia et vultum teretesque suras Integer laudo,.—
Healthy, sound, sane, unimpaired: animi,: mentis,; cf. mens,: a conjuratione,without complicity in,: integrius judicium a favore et odio,.—
New to a thing, ignorant of it: rudem me discipulum, et integrum accipe,: suffragiis integer, Dietsch—
In which nothing has yet been done, undecided, undetermined: integram rem et causam relinquere,: rem integram ad reditum suum jussit esse,: integram omnem causam reservare alicui,: ea dicam, quae ipsi, re integra saepe dixi,: ut quam integerrima ad pacem essent omnia,: offensiones,not yet cancelled,: integrum est mihi,it is still in my power, I am at liberty,: loquor de legibus promulgatis, de quibus est integrum vobis,: non est integrum, Cn. Pompeio consilio jam uti tuo,: ei ne integrum quidem erat, ut, etc.,. — So, integrum dare,to grant full power, to leave at liberty,. — Adv.: intĕgrē.
Lit., wholly, entirely: mutare,.—
Trop.
Irreproachably, honestly, justly: incorrupte atque integre judicare,: in amicorum periculis caste integreque versatus,. — Comp.: quid dici potest integrius, quid incorruptius, .— Sup.: Asiam integerrime administravit,: procuratione integerrime functus,. —
Purely, correctly: integre et ample et ornate dicere,: proprie atque integre loqui,.

la:verb:interpello.gloss: to interrupt by speaking, disrupt, disturb, interject
senses: to interrupt by speaking, disrupt, disturb, interject
to hinder, obstruct, impede, disturb, molest
to try to seduce a female, solicit
la:verb:interpello.html:
inter-pello, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to interrupt by speaking, to disturb, molest, etc. (syn. obloquor; class.).
To interrupt by speaking, to disturb a person speaking: si interpellas, ego tacebo,: nihil te interpellabo, continentem orationem audire malo,: tu vero, ut me et appelles, et interpelles, et obloquare, et colloquare, velim,: quasi interpellamur ab iis,; a person engaged in business: si quis te arti tuae intentum sic interpellet,. — Absol.: ministri, interpellando, . . . atrocitatem facti leniebant,; .—
Esp.
To annoy, importune: cum a Ceballino interpellatus sum,: urbe egrediens, ne quis se interpellaret,; molest, disturb one, . —
To solicit, try to seduce a female: qui mulierem puellamve interpellaverit, Huschke ().—
To address, accost, speak to, i. q. alloqui: verum tu quid agis? interpella me, ut sciam, Lucil. ap. ; = interjicere, interpellantem admonere,to object,. —
To dun, demand payment of, ; cf. . —
In gen., to disturb, hinder, obstruct, molest; constr. with acc., quin, quominus, ne, or inf.
With acc.; of persons: aliquem in jure suo,; of things: partam jam victoriam,: poenam,: incrementa urbis,: otium bello,: satietatem epularum ludis,: lex Julia non interpellat eam possessionem,does not disturb, does not abrogate it,.—Pass.: reperiebat T. Ampium conatum esse tollere pecunias ... sed interpellatum adventum Caesaris profugisse,: haec tota res interpellata bello refrixerat,: stupro interpellato motus,.—
With quin: Caesar numquam interpellavit, quin, quibus vellem, uterer, Matius ad .—
With quominus: interpellent me, quo minus honoratus sim, dum ne interpellent, quo minus, etc.,.—
With ne: tribunis interregem interpellantibus, ne senatusconsultum fieret, to interpose their veto, .—(ε) With inf.: pransus non avide, quantum interpellet inani Ventre diem durare,.—(ζ) Absol.: fameque et siti interpellante, disturbing him, .

la:adv:interdum.html:
inter-dum, adv.,
sometimes, occasionally, now and then, = nonnumquam: interdum fio Juppiter, quando lubet,: interdum cursus est in oratione incitatior, interdum moderata ingressio,: modo-interdum,: modo-modo-interdum,.—
I. q. per aliquod tempus, for some time (post-Aug.): acribus custodiis domum et vias saepserat Livia; laetique interdum nuntii vulgabantur, donec,: occulere interdum et terrae mandare parabat,; .—
I. q. interea, interim, meanwhile, in the meantime (post-class.): interdum cognito strepitu procurrit cubiculo,; , p. 149, 14; ; Cod. Th. 4, 3, 1.

senses: to be present, attend (+ dative), take part
to make a difference; to concern; to matter
la:verb:intersum.html:
inter-sum, fŭi, esse (interfŭtūrus, ;
in tmesi: interque esse desiderat pugnis,), v. n., to be between, lie between (class.; syn. interjaceo).
In gen.
Of space: quas (segetes) inter et castra unus omnino collis intererat,: ut Tiberis inter eos et pons interesset,: via interest perangusta,: morari victoriam rati, quod interesset amnis,: quod interest spatii,.—
Of time: cujus inter primum et sextum consulatum sex et quadraginta anni interfuerunt,elapsed,: inter Laviniam et Albam Longam coloniam deductam triginta ferme interfuere anni,; .—
Transf.
To be apart; with abl. of distance (syn. disto): clathros interesse oportet pede,.—
To be different, to differ: ut inter eos, ne minimum quidem intersit,there is not the slightest difference,: inter hominem et beluam hoc maxime interest, quod, men differ chiefly from brutes in this, that, etc., : vide, quantum interfuturum sit inter meam atque tuam accusationem,how great a difference there will be,: in his rebus nihil omnino interest,there is no difference whatever,; : hoc pater ac dominus interest,there is this difference,: tantum id interest, veneritne eo itinere ad urbem, an ab urbe in Campaniam redierit,.— With ab (like differo, rare): negant quidquam a falsis interesse,; cf.: quod intersit aut differat, aliud ab alio,: quod ab eo nihil intersit, etc.,.—With dat.: ut matrona Intererit Satyris paulum pudibunda protervis,: quid dimidium dimidiato intersit,.—With gen. (in analogy with the Gr. διαφέρειν τινός): quoniam τὸ νεμεσᾶν interest (= διαφέρει) τοῦ φθονεῖν, i. e. anger differs from envy, —
To be present at, take part in, attend; constr. absol., with dat. or in and abl.
Absol.: ac si ipse interfuerit, ac praesens viderit,: interfuisse me memini,.—
With dat. rei: consiliis,; : crudelitati,: negotiis,: lacrimis patris,: ludis,: caedi,: rebus gerendis,: sermoni,: senatui,; : populo Quirini,to be among, live with,: rebus divinis,: proelio,: bello,: spectaculo,.— Also, with dat. loci: curiae,: contubernio patris,.—Also, with dat. pers.: sacrificanti interfuit,attended him,.—
With in and abl.: in convivio,: in testamento faciendo,: voluerunt eos in suis rebus ipsos interesse,: quibus in rebus,.— Also used of time, to live in: quisquis illis temporibus interfuit,: cui tempori Saturninus interfuit,; cf.: ea (ratiocinatio) dicitur interfuisse tum, cum aliquid vitasse aut secutus esse animus videbitur,to have taken place,.—
To interest, be of interest to one (very rare as pers. verb): non quo mea interesset natura loci, (cf. interest, impers. infra). —
Esp.: intĕrest, impers., it makes a difference, interests, concerns, imports; is of interest, importance; constr. with gen. pers. or meā, tuā, suā, and with a subj. or rel. clause, ut or ne, or with ad: ea vos rata habeatis, ne magis reipublicae interest, quam mea,: quanto opere reipublicae communisque salutis intersit, manus hostium distineri,: semper ille, quantum interesset P. Clodii, se perire, cogitabat,: quid illius interest, ubi sis?: quis enim est hodie, cujus intersit istam legem manere?: hoc vehementer interest rei publicae,: quod ego et mea et rei publicae interesse arbitror,: multum interest rei familiaris tuae, te quam primum venire,: tuā et meā maxime interest, te valere,: id ignorare eos velis, quorum intersit id scire,.— With ut or ne: illud meā magni interest, te ut videam,: quod ut facias tuā interesse arbitror,: vestrā interest, ne imperatorem pessimi faciant,: non tam suā quam reipublicae interesse ut salvus esset,; so, utriusque nostrum magni interest ut te videam, B. and K. (dub.).— With gen. pretii: quod meus familiaris tanti suā interesse arbitraretur,.—With rel. or interrog.-clause: in omnibus novis conjunctionibus interest, qualis primus aditus sit,: non tam interest, quo animo scribatur, quam quo accipiatur, Caecin. ap. : neque multum interest, quod nondum per numeros distributi sunt,; cf. with utrum ... an: quid interfuit, homo audacissime, utrum hoc decerneres, an, etc., what mattered it? : nihil interest nunc, an violaverim, etc.,.— With ad: ad honorem interesse,: ad decus et ad laudem civitatis,: ad laudem nostram,: ad beate vivendum,.

la:verb:interpretor.html:
interprĕtor, ātus (in tmesi:
inter quaecumque pretantur,), 1, v. dep.
interpres
, to explain, expound, interpret, give expression to, translate; to understand, conclude, infer, appreciate, recognize, comprehend.
In gen. (class.): tuae memoriae interpretari me aequom censes,: nec quidquam aliud est philosophia, si interpretari velis, quam studium sapientiae,: jus,: monstra aut fulgura,: somnia,: sapienter,: cetera de genere hoc,: aliquid mitiorem in partem,: felicitatem alicujus grato animo, : male bene dicta,: grate beneficia,: male beneficium fortunae,: voluntatem alicujus,: sententiam alicujus,: epistolam alicujus,: qui scriptum recitet et scriptoris voluntatem non interpretetur,: medio responso spem ad voluntatem interpretantibus fecerat,: obscure dicta,: aenigmata,: leges,: versus,: ἀλληγορία, quam inversionem interpretamur, translate, ; ; : ut plerique ... viso aspectoque Agricola quaererent famam, pauci interpretarentur,few understood him,: jussa ducum interpretari quam exsequi malle,.—With inf.: reditu enim in castra, liberatum se esse jurejurando, interpretabatur,: pomoerium verbi vim solam intuentes postmoerium interpretantur esse,: victoriam ut suam,claimed as his own,: nolite consilium ex necessitate, nec voluntatem ex vi interpretari,: virtutem ex consuetudine vitae,: Chaldaeos interpretatos imperium Persarum ad eos transiturum, interpret signs, etc., i. e. predict, foretell, ; ; .—
Esp.
To decide, determine: neque, recte, an perperam, interpretor,.—
Memoriae alicujus, to assist one's memory, .—
To translate: recte sententiam (v. the context),.—
Diabolo, to ascribe to the devil, .?*! In pass. sense: scripturae, quae male de Hebraicis interpretata sunt,: ex quo ita illud somnium esse interpretatum, ut, etc.,: flumen Naarmalcha, quod amnis regum interpretatur,.— interprĕtātus, a, um, P. a., explained, translated (class.): nomen,: haec ex Graeco carmine interpretata recitavit,; .

la:noun:interpellatio.html:
interpellātĭo, ōnis, f.
interpello
,
a speaking between, an interruption in speaking; an interruption, hinderance.
In gen.: quid tibi interpellatio aut in consilium huc accessiost?What business have you to interrupt?: cursum orationis interpellatione impedire,; : sine ulla interpellatione,; : si quid nobis agentibus novi accidit, interpellatio, interventio alicujus, etc.,; ; . —
In law, a suit, appeal to the court, ; .

la:verb:intereo.gloss: to go among, become lost in
senses: to go among, become lost in
la:verb:intereo.html:
intĕr-ĕo, ĭi, ĭtum (
perf. -īvi, ; sync. -issent, ), 4, v. n.—Prop., to go among several things, so as no longer to be perceived (class.).
Lit.: ut interit magnitudine maris stilla muriae,becomes lost in it,: saxa venis, become lost among them, mingle with them, Sever. Aetn. 450. —
Trop., to perish, to go to ruin or decay, to die: non intellego, quomodo, calore exstincto, corpora intereant,: omnia fato Interitura gravi,: segetes,: salus urbis,: litterae,: pecunia,: interit ira morā,ceases,: possessio,.—
To be ruined, mostly in first pers. perf.: interii, I am ruined, undone: hei mihi disperii! ... interii, perii,: omnibus exitiis interii,: interii! cur mihi id non dixti?: qui per virtutem peritat, non interit,.— Hence, intĕrĭtus, a, um, Part., perished, destroyed (ante- and post-class.): multis utrinque interitis, Claud. Quadrig. ap. P.; .

la:noun:interitus.html:
intĕrĭtus, ūs, m.
intereo
,
destruction, ruin, annihilation (class.): interitus est quasi discessus et secretio, ac diremptio earum rerum, quae junctione aliqua tenebantur,: omnium rerum interitus atque obitus,: legum,: exercitus,: pravitatis,: immaturus,i. e. death,: tuum ingemuisse interitum,: vitae,.

la:verb:interficio.html:
interfĭcĭo, fēci, fectum (archaic
pass.: interfiat,: interfieri,), 3, v. a.
inter-facio
, to put between.
In gen. (rare): terrae natura medicatas aquas interficit, (al. inficiat).—
In partic.
To consume, devour: piscium magnam atque altilium vim, Lucil. ap. —
To destroy, bring to naught: messes,: herbas, ap. : usum, fructum, victum,: virginitatem,.—
To kill, slay, murder (class.; syn. neco, occido, trucido): aliquem,; ; ; ; : feras,.—With abl. of separation, to cut off from: aliquem et vitā, et lumine,.—With abl. of means: anum siti fameque atque algu,.—
Esp. with se, to commit suicide: se ipsum, Sulp. ap. : omnes desperatā salute se ipsi interficiunt,; ; ; ; ; ; , 1, 17 fin. al.—*
To interrupt: sermonem,.

la:verb:intexo.html:
in-texo, texŭi, textum, 3, v. a.,
to weave into, to inweave, interweave; to plait, join together, interlace, surround, cover.
Lit.: purpureasque notas filis intexuit albis,: diversos colores picturae,: hastas foliis,: vitibus ulmos,: vestibus intexto Phrygiis spectabilis auro,; cf. : cum chlamyde purpurea variis coloribus intexta,embroidered,: intextus puer regius,; : hederae intexere truncos,.—
Esp., to weave, make by weaving or interlacing: tribus intextum tauris opus,of hides,: sterili junco cannaque intexta palustri,: ex lino,; cf.: latera intextus stellatis axibus agger,.—
Trop.: facta chartis, to interweave on paper, i. e. to describe, : parva magnis, laeta tristibus,: aliquid in causa prudenter,: Varronem,: tali te vellem ritu inter soles ... naturae rerum magnis intexere chartis, to interweave in a poem on nature your fame, etc., .

la:verb:intego.html:
in-tĕgo, xi, ctum, 3, v. a.,
to cover: villam,: turres coriis,: reliqua pars scrobis viminibus ac virgultis integebatur,: cum prima luce densa nebula saltum camposque intexit,; : casside crines,: Clitumnus flumina luco Integit, (3, 12), 25: statuas auro,: viam, to arch over, Inscr. ap. Grut. 150, 1.—
To protect: vidit cum loci altitudine tum vallo etiam integi Romanos, Weissenb. ad loc.

la:adj:intemperans.html:
in-tempĕrans, antis, adj.,
intemper,ate, immoderate.
Lit.: intemperans atque immoderata permixtio,.— Comp., .—
Trop.
That cannot govern himself, without moderation, extravagant, immoderate, intemperate: intemperantis esse arbitror scribere, quod occultari velit,: fui paulo intemperantior fortasse, quam debui,i. e. I ought to have exhibited more moderation,: intemperans sum in ejus rei cupiditate,: intemperans militaris in forti viro gloria,: in augendo eo non alius intemperantior est,: avidi atque intemperantes animi,: in voluptates,: ad vescendum,.—
Incontinent, profligate, debauched: inter impudicas mulieres, et intemperantes viros versari,: libidinosa et intemperans adulescentia,: impurissima atque intemperantissima pecus,.—Adv.: intempĕranter, immoderately, extravagantly, intemperately: nimis iracunde hoc quidem, et valde intemperanter,: intemperanter abuti et otio et litteris,

: lacerare aliquem,.— Comp.: ne intemperantius opibus suis utatur,: insequi,: amare,: adesse adversus aliquem. .— Sup.: intemperantissime gloriari,.

la:verb:intermitto.html:
inter-mitto, mīsi, missum, 3, v. a. and n.
Act.
To leave off, intermit, omit, neglect; constr. with acc., aliquid ab, ad, or inf.
With acc.: studia,: iter,: proelium,: opus,: admirationem rerum,: officia militaria,: curam rerum,: laborem,: quod (otium) quidem paulisper intermisit,; cf.: qua erat nostrum opus intermissum,.—
Aliquid ab: ut reliquum tempus a labore intermitteretur,: tempus ab opere,; cf. . —
With ad: nulla pars nocturni temporis ad laborem intermittitur,; .—(ε) With inf.: quod tu mihi litteras mittere intermisisses,; so, non intermittit suo tempore caelum mitescere, etc.,: consulere rei publicae,; : obsides dare,. —
To let pass, suffer to elapse: tempus, quin,: unum diem, quin veniat,: diem,. —
Neutr.
To leave off, cease, pause: gallos gallinaceos sic assidue canere coepisse, ut nihil intermitterent,: aves intermittentes bibunt,drink by separate draughts,.—
To leave an interval, to pause: spatium, qua flumen intermittit,does not flow,; : febris intermittit,is intermittent,: febris intermittens,an intermitting fever,.—Hence, intermissus, a, um, Part.
Of a place, not occupied by, free from: custodiis loca,; : planities intermissa collibus,.—
Of time or space, permitted to elapse, intervening, left between.
Of time: brevi tempore intermisso,.—
Of space: intermissis circiter passibus quadringentis,; —
Intermitted, neglected, or omitted for a time, respited, interrupted: ludi,: ventus,: libertas,: impetus remorum,: bella,: bellum,: censura diu,: nono die, intermisso rure, ad mercatum venire, Rutil. ap. . —
Not surrounded, unenclosed: pars oppidi, quae intermissa a flumine et a paludibus: aditum angustum habebat,: trabes intermissae spatiis,separated,: verba prisca et ab usu quotidiani sermonis jamdiu intermissa,i. e. given up, abandoned,: ordo,: mos,: per intermissa moenia urbem intrārunt,i. e. where the wall was discontinued,: facies, non multarum imaginum et intermissarum, sed unius longae et continuae,.—
Left out, omitted (late Lat.): nonnulla, quae mihi intermissa videbantur, adjeci, Hier. praef. ad Chron. Euseb.
la:verb:intermitto.inflection: mīsi, missum, 3, v. a. and n.

la:verb:intervenio.html:
inter-vĕnĭo, vēni, ventum, 4, v. n., rarely
a., to come between, come upon, to come in during, to intervene, interrupt (class.; syn. intercedo).
Lit., constr. with dat., rarely with acc.
Of persons: sponsae pater intervenit,: quin malo abscedas: ne interveneris, quaeso, dum resipiscit,: verens ne molesti vobis interveniremus,: casu Germani equites interveniunt,: orationi,: Statius intervenit nonnullorum querelis,.— With pro: pro sociis,. — With ne: ne quid perperam fieret,. —
Of things.
To come, be, or lie between: medius paries intervenit,: interveniente Ascanio lacu,: interveniente flumine,; .—
To interfere with, interrupt, put a stop to.
With dat.: nox proelio intervenit,: continuationi sermonis,: verboque intervenit omni plangor,; so, of an oath in conversation: quoties lascivum intervenit illud, etc., .—
With acc. (only in Tacitus): ludorum diebus, qui cognitionem intervenerant,.—
Transf.
To take place meanwhile or among other things, to happen, occur: nulla mihi res posthac potest jam intervenire tanta, quae, etc.,: quae inter vos intervenerint, etc.,: Epicurus exiguam dicit fortunam intervenire sapienti,: casus mirificus quidam intervenit,has taken place,: interveniunt motu stellarum grandines, imbres,: intervenit his cogitationibus avitum malum, regni cupido,.—
To stand in the way of, to oppose, hinder, prevent, disturb: Sabinum bellum coeptis intervenit,: deliberationi metum pro republica intervenisse,: vilicum intervenientem flagellāsset,: quis vestro Deus intervenit amori?.—
Leg. t. t.
To interpose, become surety, ; —
To conduct a suit in another's name, ; cf. 4, 86 init.: pro debitore,.—
To interfere, intermeddle, exercise one's authority: neque senatu interveniente,: praetor interveniet,. — Pass. impers.: si interventum est casu,: ubi de improviso est interventum mulieri,.

la:verb:intero.html:

la:verb:interpono.html:
inter-pōno, pŏsŭi, pŏsĭtum, 3, v. a.,
to put, place, lay, or set between or among, to interpose, insert between.
Lit.
Of place, constr. with acc. and dat., or inter with acc.: equitatus praesidia levis armaturae,; ; : vestibus interponi eam (herbam) gratissimum,: ubi spatium inter muros ... pilae interponuntur,: inter eos levis armaturae Numidas,: uti levis armatura interjecta inter equites suos interponeretur,: sulcos,: ne interpositi quidem elephanti militem deterrebant,: lateri vinculum lapides sunt, quos interposuere, ut, etc.,.—
Esp.
To insert, interpose, introduce.—Of time: intercalariis mensibus interpositis,; cf.: inediam unius diei per singulos menses,.—Of musical notes: iis sonis quos interposuerant, inserunt alios,.—Of words or language: ne inquam et inquit saepius interponeretur,: hoc loco libet interponere ... quantae, etc.,: subinde interponenti precibus, quid respondebo,

etc., : paucis interpositis versibus,: aliquid,: verbum ullum,; so, querelas,: meam sententiam, — Of a letter in a word: quibusdam (verbis litteram),.—Of a foot in verse: quibusdam (iambus) interpositus,.—

Of time, to let pass, permit to elapse, leave an interval: spatium ad recreandos animos,: ejus rei causa moram interponi arbitrabatur,, fin.: tridui mora interposita,after a delay of,; ; ; : nullam moram,: nullam moram, quin, etc.,: spatio interposito,some time after,; : diebus aliquot interpositis,: tempore interposito,; cf. ; : hac interposita nocte,.—
To mingle: frigidam (cibis),to drink cold water while eating,; cf.: condimentis cuminum,to mix with,.—
With personal objects, to introduce among, admit among, bring into, to bring into a feast, a society, among associates, etc.: quam sancta sit societas civium, dis immortalibus interpositis, etc.,: aliquem convivio,: legatos familiaribus,. —
Trop., to interpose, introduce, put in the way, put forward.
In gen., as a hinderance, interference, reason, or pretext: Lentulus provinciam, quam sorte habebat, interposita religione, deposuit,: neque ulla belli suspicione interposita,: nulla interposita dubitatione,; ; : interposita pactione,: offensione aliqua interposita,: nec colloquium interposita causa tolli volebat,; : causam interponens collegas exspectare,: postulata haec ab eo interposita esse, quominus, etc.,: operam, studium, laborem pro sociis,.—
Esp.
Of a judgment, decree, edict, oath, etc.: jurejurando interposito,; : jus eo die se non dicturum, neque decretum interpositurum,: ad decreta interponenda pecuniam occipere,; : judicium suum,: poenas compromissaque,: exceptionem actioni,: intercessionem suam (of a tribune of the people),: tutor interponit auctoritatem suam,gives his authorization,. —
Fidem interponere, to pledge one's word or credit: fidem suam in eam rem,: fidem reliquis interponere, jusjurandum poscere, ut, etc.,: fidem suam in re omni,: omni interposita fide,: ut in eam rem fidem suam, si quid opus esse putaret, interponeret,; cf.: sponsio interponeretur,.—
Se interponere (in aliquid, or alicui rei; also with quominus or absol.), to interfere, intermeddle, engage in, set one's self in the way: si te in istam pacificationem non interponis,: bello se,: num ego me non interpono Romanis,: num quem putas posse reperiri, qui se interponat, quominus, etc.?: quid enim me interponerem audaciae tuae?expose myself,: ni tribuni plebis interposuissent se,: tu vero, quod voles, facies; me nihil interpono,.— Rarely, to interfere, interpose in behalf of any one: semper se interposuit,; : Qui me mediis interposuerim Caesaris scriptis, i.e. by writing a continuation,

inter-clūdo, ūsi, ūsum, 3, v. a.
claudo
,

Lit.
To cut off, hinder, stop, block up, shut off.
Of one's way, passage, entrance, retreat, etc.; constr. (syn. intersaepio).
With acc. of thing and dat. of person: hisce omnis aditus ad Sullam,: sibi reditum,; cf. also: intercludit aditum veritati,.— Esp. freq. in milit. lang.: iter inimicis,: exitum Romano,: aditum Romanis,.—
With gen. of person (very rare): multitudinis fugam,.—
Pass., with abl. of thing: his superatis aut reditu interclusis,: omni exitu interclusi,: interclusus itinere Caesar,; ; : ne reditu intercluderentur, Auct. B. Alex. 20, 5; but with abl. of manner, etc.: via inculta atque interclusa frondibus et virgultis,: cum Byzantii totum Pontum aegre repulsum, et cervicibus interclusum suis, sustinerent,.—
With acc. alone: bene laudata virtus voluptatis aditus intercludat necesse est,; cf.: omnīs vias seditionum,: ut fugam intercludat,: iter,, D. 4: fugam,: illos aspera ponti Interclusit hiemps,: cervis objectis, ut viam intercluderet,: exitum ad opem ferendam,.—
In gen., to shut off, cut off, stop, hinder, prevent: commeatus hostibus,; : ob interclusos commeatus,: spiritum,; : vocem,; cf.: consuli admiratio intercluserat vocem,.—
To cut off, separate one from any thing.
From a place.
With acc., ab, and abl. (so most usu.): adversarios ab oppido,: Pompeium ab eo (Dyrrachio),: ipsum ab reliquo exercitu, Cael. ap. : so, ab exercitu,: a praesidio,: intercludi ab oppido,: interclusi ab suis,: a patria,: ab acie,: tribunos a plebe, et saep.; Auct. B. Alex. 27, 4; . —
With acc. and abl. alone (rare): hostem Hibero intercludere, et frumento prohibere (cf. 2. infra),.—
From aid, supplies, relief, etc.; with abl.: re frumentaria intercludi,: frumento commeatuque Caesarem,: commeatibus nostros. ; ; : ille commeatu et reliquis copiis intercludendus,: hostem commeatibus,: hostes commeatibus in urbe inclusos intercludunt,.—Absol.: ne tot fortissimos viros interclusos opprimeret hostis,; cf.: interclusi equites, § 2.—
To shut in, blockade: metuo, ne jam intercludemur, ut cum velitis exire, non liceat,: libertatem suis praesidiis interclusam tenere,: veriti, ne angustiis intercluderentur,: aliquem in insidiis,: animam,to stop the breath, to stifle,: Amazoniā latus peltā,to cover,. —
Trop., to hinder, prevent; with quominus: intercludor dolore, quominus ad te plura scribam,.
